title: Latency SLO Driftboard: side-by-side streaming vs non-streaming breakdown and request-path attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a single-pane Driftboard for product and SRE teams that compares latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across model routes and explicitly decomposes streaming vs non-streaming request handling. The board must surface attribution by request path (ingress/front proxy, routing, runtime kernel, KV cache hits/misses, and network egress), include an expected-baseline synthetic overlay, and link to sampled traces and raw logs for fast TTR. This work stitches together tracing hooks, the OTLP/metrics pipeline, and Grafana dashboard panels. Key goals: fast root-cause for regressions, automated SLO drift detection, and support for filtered views by model variant, quantization profile, and deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private).
acceptance_criteria: Driftboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model route and time window
Streaming and non-streaming lines shown side-by-side with shared y-axis and selectable percentiles
Waterfall-style decomposition panel attributing median and tail latency to: ingress, routing, runtime queue, kernel execution, kv-cache, and egress
Synthetic baseline overlay available per-model (configurable) to highlight drift > 15%
Click-to-open trace links (sampled) from any percentile point with trace id propagation (frontend -> runtime) working end-to-end
Metrics and logs powering the board go through the OTLP -> metrics pipeline with <30s ingestion lag in prod region
Alerts (p95/p99) can be attached to model-route SLOs with automatic paging and a Runbook link
Dashboard supports comparisons across model variants and quantization profiles (e.g., fp16 vs int8) for the same route
Query performance: panels refresh under 2s for 1h windows in our Lille and us-east regions
Documentation and playbook added to Confluence and linked from the dashboard
